**Verified answer:** 64

**Check.** For a monic degree-6 polynomial with all roots $r_i\in(0,1)$, the product of the roots is $P=f(0)=\prod r_i>0$. The condition $f(0)=f(1)$ gives $\prod(1-r_i)=P$. Multiplying these gives $P^2=\prod r_i(1-r_i)\le (1/4)^6$ by AM–GM, so $P\le 1/64$ and $1/P\ge 64$.

**Attainment.** $f(x)=(x-\tfrac12)^6$ has all roots equal to $\tfrac12\in(0,1)$ and $f(0)=f(1)=\tfrac1{64}$. Its root product is $\tfrac1{64}$, so the reciprocal is exactly 64.

The submitted value 1 falls below the proven lower bound of 64, so it cannot be the minimum.
